dialog.body: Public Works, Denise speaking, how can I help?

Hi, yeah, Denise, hi. You're on speaker, sorry, I've got my hands full here. This is Paul Pucci, I'm calling about my mother's house, 701 Thames Street, down the Fifth Ward end, by the corner there. The drain on the corner. Again.
Okay, Paul. I think I talked to your mom yesterday morning, actually. Give me one second, I'll pull it up.

Yeah, she called Tuesday. She told me she called. But I wanted to, you know, I wanted to make sure, because, honestly, the last time I called, in January, it was the same thing. Somebody said a crew's gonna come look at the drain, and, uh...
Mm-hm.

And nobody looked at the drain. A truck came, they swept the leaves off the grate on top, and they left. That's it. Nobody looked at the pipe. My wife even called back after that and said, hey, it's still backing up under the street, and then nothing. And now here we are, Sunday night, the whole corner's a pond, and the basement's got four inches in it. That's twice this winter. Twice! January and now this.
I hear you. Okay, I've got it. Your mom's call yesterday, Tuesday the twenty-fourth, repeat backup at 701 Thames. I've got your January call too, the tenth, and your wife's on the twelfth.

Right, the January storm, that was the first one. Three inches that time. Washer and dryer got soaked. And then this nor'easter, Saturday into Sunday, and Sunday night, boom, same thing, worse. We had to shut the breaker off down there. My mother's sixty-nine, she's not supposed to be wading around in a basement with the, the... sorry, hold on, I've got this thing on my screen. [pause] There's a pop-up. I was trying to look at the city website while I'm on with you and there's this pop-up, some survey or something, and I can't get rid of it. There's no X. I keep hitting it. [laughs] Okay, forget it. Where was I?
Your mom in the basement.
Right, yeah. [laughs] Sorry. Anyway, so what I wanna know is, is somebody actually coming this time? Like actually coming, not sweeping leaves?

Yes. There's a crew booked for tomorrow, Thursday, in the afternoon, sometime after noon. That's still on the schedule, I'm looking at it. And I put in for a supervisor to call your mom back on her cell. That hasn't happened yet, but it's in.
Okay. Tomorrow afternoon. And they know it's the pipe, not the grate? Because the grate's fine. The grate's been fine since January. It's whatever's under there.
The note says repeat backup, grate was cleared January twelfth, problem's below the street. I'll add that you called today and that the family's asking for the line itself to be checked.
Please. Because, I mean, no offense, Denise, but we did this already. It's the same story.
None taken. You've called three times, I'd be fed up too.

Yeah. [crosstalk] ...and the other thing. Can I ask, the next storm, can the city put one of those pump trucks on the corner? Like, just park it there? Because whatever they find tomorrow, they're not fixing a pipe under Thames Street by Saturday, right?
Sorry, you broke up a little. A pump truck at the corner during the next storm?
Yeah. Just park it there and pump the corner before it gets in the house.

That's not something I can promise from this desk. During a storm the trucks get sent wherever it's worst. But I'll put the request on the work order, and that's a good one to ask the supervisor when they call your mom.

Okay. And, uh, can you put us on a list or something? Like, before the next storm comes, somebody calls us, gives us a heads up, hey, we're coming, or hey, we're not, move your stuff. Because we got shelves down there, my mother's got stuff on them, and we're moving it every time it rains. [laughs] We're getting good at it, which is not a good thing.
I can flag it for a callback before the next forecasted storm. I can't tell you who'll call, but it'll be on the file. Do you want it to go to your number or your mom's?
Mine. She's at work, she doesn't pick up. It's 401-555-0188.
401-555-0188, Paul Pucci. Got it. So, crew tomorrow after noon, supervisor callback to your mom still pending, pump truck request noted, and a pre-storm callback to you.
Okay. That's, yeah, that's everything. I think. [laughs] I had a list and the pop-up ate it. Oh, it's gone now. Figures.
Of course it is. If the crew doesn't show by end of day tomorrow, call me Friday morning.
Oh, I will. Believe me. Thanks, Denise.
You're welcome, Paul. Take care.
